verses.text: You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach others as well.
Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.
Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.
The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.
Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel,
for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God cannot be chained!
For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
This is a trustworthy saying: If we died with Him, we will also live with Him;
if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us;
if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.
Make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.
But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness,
and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
who have deviated from the truth. They say that the resurrection has already occurred, and they undermine the faith of some.
Nevertheless, God's firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: "The Lord knows those who are His," and, "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity."
A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.
So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.
Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.
And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing.
He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.
Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.

context.author: Paul the apostle (1:1)
context.setting: Paul tells Timothy to be strong in grace and entrust what he has learned to faithful people who will teach others. He gives three pictures of faithful work: soldier, athlete, farmer. He warns about word-battles and urges Timothy to correct opponents gently.
context.custom: Soldiers had one aim: to please the commander. Athletes had to compete by the rules to win the crown. A farmer who works hard gets the first share of crops. Each pictures an aspect of faithfulness.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 3 describes dangers of the last days.
context.timelineBible: The hymn-like “If we died with him, we will also live with him” (vv.11-13) is an early Christian saying. “Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity” (v.19) echoes Numbers 16:5 and Isaiah 52:11.
context.sparkNotes: Be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus, and entrust what you heard to faithful men who will teach others. Share in suffering as a good soldier. An athlete is not crowned unless he competes by the rules. A hard-working farmer should have the first share of the crops. Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead. Do your best to be a worker who handles the word of truth rightly. The Lord’s servant must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone.

translation.meaning: To cut straight, as a road, a stonecutter’s line, or a tentmaker’s seam.

otBackground.note: The Lord knows who are his.

overview.summary: Timothy is to pass on the faith, endure like a soldier, athlete, and farmer, rightly handle the word of truth, and correct opponents gently.
overview.settingLine: Paul writes from prison, near the end of his life.

history.t: Paul tells Timothy to entrust what he heard from Paul among many witnesses to faithful people who will be able to teach others as well (2:2). That makes four stages in handing on the message: Paul, Timothy, the faithful people, and those they teach.

Paul names two teachers who have departed from the truth by saying the resurrection has already taken place (2:17-18). First Timothy 1:20 names a Hymenaeus together with Alexander, but the letters do not say they are the same man. Some scholars think the claim was that the resurrection was spiritual, as in baptism; Paul does not explain it.

customs.t: Paul asks Timothy to endure hardship like a good soldier (2:3) and says a soldier avoids civilian entanglements to please the one who enlisted him (2:4). Paul also calls Epaphroditus and Archippus "fellow soldier" (Philippians 2:25; Philemon 2). Roman soldiers swore an oath and lived under strict military discipline.

Paul says an athlete is crowned only if he competes according to the rules (2:5). Greek games had strict rules and officials. The Greek travel writer Pausanias (2nd century AD) says athletes at Olympia swore they had trained for ten months. Paul does not mention that; his point is that the prize goes to the one who keeps the rules.

archaeology.t: Bronze military diplomas were small folded bronze tablets given to soldiers of auxiliary units and fleets on discharge, recording a grant of Roman citizenship. The earliest known date from the reign of Claudius, and most surviving ones are from the 2nd century AD, later than Paul.

Prizes at the Greek games varied: olive at Olympia, laurel at Delphi, pine at Isthmia and celery at Nemea, and at the Panathenaic Games a jar of olive oil. Paul's picture of the athlete who receives the crown (2:5) uses a word from the same family as the crown of righteousness in 4:8.

overview.discussion: Paul uses three images for faithful service. Which one is most like my current season: soldier, athlete, or farmer?
overview.book: The second letter to Timothy · 4 chapters. Paul’s last words, written from prison with death in view.

currentImage.caption: The ancient stadium at Ephesus, where athletic contests were held in the Roman period. Paul uses the athlete (2 Timothy 2:5) and the finished race (4:7) as pictures of faithful service.
